A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the RoBBR benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions to coverage and evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on four benchmark tasks and a human-versus-GPT annotation agreement study, with additional results and standard errors in Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning results, annotation comparisons, retrieval interventions, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V2 adds retrieval-conditioned inference variants: risk classification from retrieved sentences and classification from the full paper with highlighted evidence (Sections 6.3–6.4). These are limited procedural extensions; the central GPT-4 annotation and distractor-generation procedures retain their existing prompts and sliding-window approach. Omission of v1's separate negation-filter prompt does not establish whether that underlying filtering step changed.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates four tasks using Cochrane-derived data. V2 removes study inclusion/exclusion and adds a non-Cochrane main-task test set containing 2,489 judgments from 496 reviews. It explicitly includes RoB2 assessments, including deviation bias and the 'some concern' label, substantially changing represented sources and assessment coverage.

E2.justification: V2 removes Claude3-Opus and Gemini-1.5-Pro from the retained task comparisons. It adds Llama-3.1-70B, untuned and fine-tuned Llama-3-8B, OpenAI-v3 and GritLM retrieval baselines, and logistic regression, SVM, and RobotReviewer comparisons. Sonnet-3.5 also joins the retrieval comparison, where v1 did not report it.

E3.justification: V2 replaces v1's capped evaluation subsets with revised task sets, including a reported 465-example SJS evaluation versus 310 previously. It changes overall reporting from pooled 'Full' scores to averages across bias categories, drops retrieval@3 and main-task accuracy/weighted accuracy, and adds task-specific fine-tuning and a restricted binary-label RobotReviewer protocol. Appendix Table 14 inconsistently retains older SJS sample counts.

E4.justification: V2 adds cross-task association analysis (Figure 4), controlled retrieval/reasoning combinations (Table 6), non-Cochrane evidence highlighting (Table 7), local-versus-global context analysis (Appendix F), and a detailed reasoning-error case study (Appendix G). These substantially extend v1's descriptive task comparisons and brief illustrative example.

E5.justification: Both versions already report bootstrapped standard errors and annotation-agreement hypothesis tests. V2 additionally reports explicitly labeled 95% confidence intervals in Tables 6–8. Its appendix benchmark tables retain per-category standard errors but omit uncertainty for aggregate scores that v1 supplied. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The benchmark result tables are substantially replaced, with screening results removed and numerous new model and analysis results added. For example, v2 Table 3 reports Llama-3-8B retrieval scores of 22.7% before fine-tuning and 40.8% afterward; Table 6 reports 31.5% versus 46.1% for GPT-4o reasoning using Sonnet-retrieved versus ground-truth sentences. Changed datasets and aggregation prevent interpreting headline v1-to-v2 differences as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2's coverage definition and Equation 1 make the existing aspect-matching guidance and Bias Recall@Optimal metric explicit, renaming the latter Aspect Recall Ratio@Optimal. They do not establish a substantively different mathematical construction. Neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 presents four tasks simulating the review process and emphasizes models falling short of expert performance. V2 centers one risk-labeling task and claims novelty specifically for its two diagnostic subtasks. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion emphasize evidence that retrieval and reasoning capabilities affect risk assessment, substantially redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: V2 develops interpretations about retrieval bottlenecks, global context, and traditional models' generalization limits, while qualifying some reasoning and baseline comparisons as inconclusive. It adds licensing, English-language coverage, and over-reliance limitations. V1's explicit caveats about expert-label errors, reviewer disagreement, and exclusion of observational studies are removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds model snapshots, generation settings, annotation costs, annotator-training details, retrieval-intervention prompts, and LoRA training details including hardware, rank, batch size, optimizer, and schedule. These materially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v1's explicit collection date and review-level split-construction description are omitted; the principal repository and licensing disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V2 replaces much of the broad screening, retrieval, and summarization survey with focused risk-labeling and support-sentence discussions. It adds work including Dias et al.'s RoBIn and contextual embedding research, and explicitly distinguishes its subtasks and annotation pipeline from prior label prediction, quotation extraction, and embedding methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before benchmark development, the four-task narrative becomes a main-task/two-subtask hierarchy, and existing task explanations and illustrations move into reorganized appendices. Terminology is standardized around SSR and SJS.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document to two columns, redraws the reviewer-process illustration, adds an annotation-pipeline diagram and analytical plots, and substantially restructures result and dataset tables. Existing task illustrations move to the appendix, while the screening illustration is removed. Many prompt images are retained unchanged despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the benchmark's diagnostic purpose. Broader data sources and baseline families address v1's narrow empirical evaluation, while retrieval interventions and error analyses provide direct evidence connecting the subtasks to risk assessment. Added implementation details improve reproducibility. Benefits outweigh remaining weaknesses, including inconsistent SJS sample counts, removed label-quality caveats, and the limited practical interpretation of gold-label-guided highlighting.
